Title: [from] “The Borealis Eclipse”
Author: by Cathryn Free
Content: “Are you ready, Jedidiah?”
“Yes, sir!”
“Then fire up those engines!” Professor Valgorium fluttered down the ladder from the main deck and stood behind the helm. His eyes barely peeked over it, and his top hat sat askew.
Jedidiah ran to the thrusters, grabbed the handle, and heaved down with all his might. A loud grinding sound filled the air.
The engine coughed.
It sputtered.
Then roared as the giant mechanical wings flapped to life. With a jolt, the flying machine lifted into the air.
“It works!” shouted Jedidiah, nearly spitting out the gum he was always chewing. The massive balloon above them lifted up, as the wings provided thrust and speed. The ground dwindled beneath them.
“It works!” The professor squeaked and tumbled over in excitement. The steering wheel spun out of control, and Jedidiah rushed over to stop it.
“The Borealis Eclipse is up and ready for business!” squealed the Professor, spinning in circles like a turtle on its back.

Jedidiah grinned and turned the helm `text(one degree)` to the left. Professor Valgorium had always been excitable, ever since Jedidiah had known him, but he had never seen the professor this exhilarated.
London shrunk down to a model size, the spires of the great city standing up like toothpicks in the sky. Smoke rose from chimneys in little gray puffs.

The sky was dappled with bright sunshine and puffy white clouds. They soared through the air, next to birds who squawked in surprise. The engine hummed, and the wind tugged at the ropes that tied the giant balloon to the main deck.

Professor Valgorium sprang back to his feet. His top hat toppled to `text(one)` side. “This is it, Jedidiah! This is the most magnificent thing the world has ever seen!” He ran to the stern of the ship, spread out his short, stubby arms, and yelled, “What a time to be alive!”
Jedidiah laughed. He kept his hands on the wheel, adjusting according to the compass mounted on the dash in front of the massive helm.

The helm was salvaged from an old steamer ship. Most of the parts of the machine had been pieced together from retired ocean liners, junked steam engine trains, and even old gas lines that were being torn up and replaced with power lines for electric lights. As his apprentice and ward, Jedidiah had spent the last `text(year and a half)` constructing this monstrous machine alongside Professor Valgorium. This moment was stupendous.
Jedidiah’s mouth hurt from smiling so much.
“Turn her north!” Professor Valgorium bellowed, waving his arms like a windmill.
Jedidiah nodded and slowly spun the helm, tick by tick.
The flying machine obeyed and tipped its nose to the right, heading north, away from the city.
They soared through the air, coasting like feathers on the wind. Jedidiah shut his eyes and drew in a deep, satisfied breath.
Then the Borealis Eclipse lurched.
Jedidiah stumbled. He slammed into the helm. The machine jerked.
Professor Valgorium shrieked as he fell back down the steps from the stern onto the main deck.
“What was that?” he cried.
Jedidiah shook his head and inspected the gauges on the dash. Everything was normal except . . .
“Professor!” he shouted.
Professor Valgorium scurried over to Jedidiah, who pointed at the fuel gauge. The little golden arrow, which had been on full, was dropping quickly.
Too quickly.
“We’re running out of fuel!” Jedidiah nearly choked on his chewing gum.
“Great Scott!” Professor Valgorium’s hat toppled over again. “How can that be?”
The machine lurched, dropping several `text(feet)` in altitude. Jedidiah’s stomach sprung into his throat. “We’re losing too much fuel!”
“There’s an extra tank of petrol under the deck on the starboard side.” Professor Valgorium took the helm. “I’ll take us back to London. You fill up the tank!”
Jedidiah sprinted over the deck and yanked on the metal ring of a trapdoor. Underneath was a hold filled with spare parts, stacks of folded canvas, and a large, heavy can of petrol.
Jedidiah heaved the can up and lugged it over to the engine.
The sound of the engine roared in his ears as he unscrewed the top of the fuel tank with shaking hands.
Steady now! he told himself.
He poured petrol into the tank, glug after glug, until the entire can was empty.
“Done!” he shouted to Professor Valgorium.
The engine hummed pleasantly again. Relief washed over Jedidiah, as he sank against the fuel tank.
